column1: # DIGESTION TRUTH SET -- hand-curated expected digestion products
# Built 2026-09-17 from the primary literature gathered in
# WHAT THIS IS. One row per (enzyme x substrate x glycoform) case whose answer
# is published and unambiguous. These are the EXPECTATIONS. Running them against
# mzLib says where the digester falls short; they are not a description of what
# it currently does. Written before slice 2, deliberately.
#   sequence          bare one-letter sequence, no glycans
#   expected_products '|'-separated, in N-to-C order; '*' marks a glycosylated
#                     residue; a single product means NO cleavage
#   expected_cuts     number of peptide bonds the enzyme severs
#   efficiency        full | reduced:<pct> | none -- 'reduced' cases are REAL
#                     cleavages that a rule engine should model as missed
#   grade             A = controlled substrate panel (kinetics or % completion)
#                     B = proteomics-scale observation on a defined substrate
#                     C = single observation, or derived by composing two rules
#   basis             observed = the paper reports this exact digest
#                     derived  = composed from published per-enzyme rules
#   known_gap         '-' means the digester is expected to get this right TODAY.
#                     Anything else names a KNOWN shortfall; the test reports
#                     Inconclusive rather than failing, so the gap stays visible
#                     without reddening CI. Clearing a reason turns that row into a
#                     real assertion -- that is how this file drives the work.
#   Tn        GalNAc alone (the tumour-associated Tn antigen)
#   T/core1   Gal-GalNAc (the T antigen; some papers write 'TF')
#   core2     Gal-GalNAc with a GlcNAc branch at O6
#   OGlcNAc   beta-O-GlcNAc (NOT mucin-type) OMan  O-mannose (NOT mucin-type)
# NOTE ON THE NEGATIVES. Rows with expected_cuts=0 are the point of this file.
# mzLib's current StcE entry is sequence-only and will cleave several of them.
# That over-digestion is exactly what slice 2 has to stop, and it is why the
# proteases.tsv comment block already admits the entries "OVER-DIGEST relative

The canonical StcE bond, stated verbatim: "StcE cleaved a synthetic peptide containing a single GalNAc, converting RPPIT*QSSL to RPPIT*Q". Motif T5-Q6-S7: glycan at P2, cut before P1'. ONE glycan, NO mucin context -- this is the case that retires any glycan-density requirement.

Same backbone as STCE-01, one sugar swapped. "StcE did not cleave the same peptide sequence containing beta-GlcNAc instead of alpha-GalNAc." The requirement is anomer- and sugar-specific, not "any O-glycan". mzLib today cleaves this.
column13: STRUCTURE-LEVEL GLYCAN. The requirement resolves to a glycosylation CLASS, and beta-O-GlcNAc genuinely IS O-linked, so it satisfies an O-glycan requirement that the real enzyme refuses. Needs monosaccharide composition on Modification -- neither mzLib nor MetaMorpheus models it.

column12: Deglycosylation abolishes activity. The baseline over-digestion case: mzLib's sequence-only StcE cleaves this today.
Elaborated core 2 at P2 does not impede cleavage. P1' (S6) is BARE -- direct evidence that a P1' glycan is not required.
Same bond as STCE-04 with a glycan ALSO at P1'. Pairs with STCE-04 to pin CR071: P1' glycosylation is permitted, never required.
StcE scores '-' on all three glycoforms of this backbone. A glycosylated T with an adjacent S is NOT sufficient; note this also bounds the no-spacer variant (STCE-07).

StcE is able to cleave sequences in which the spacer X is missing, although it does so less efficiently. Observed on PSGL-1, not on a defined synthetic peptide, so no exact product list is defensible. Encode as a REDUCES rule, not a truth-set row.

THE MISSING READ-THROUGH, encoded so it cannot be forgotten. An O-glycan at Thr5 is VARIABLE: the sample contains molecules that carry it and molecules that do not. StcE cuts the first population and cannot cut the second, so a correct digest contains all three species -- the two cut products AND the intact peptide from the unglycosylated molecules. Today the intact form is missing: the occupancy gate drops the peptidoform whose cut is unjustified, but nothing generates the read-through that should replace it, because at MaxMissedCleavages = 0 that peptide was never enumerated. This is the exact case the site-list feasibility filter CANNOT catch, because the site IS feasible -- it is merely unoccupied in this peptidoform.
column13: MISSING READ-THROUGH after an occupancy drop. The two-stage correction handles feasibility at site-finding time, which needs no slack, but the per-peptidoform occupancy gate has no replacement peptide for what it removes. Fixing it needs generation slack bounded by how many feasible-but-unoccupied sites a peptidoform can contain -- the promoting analogue of what #1119 does with MaxMods. Clearing this flag is the acceptance test for that work.

SmE cleaves N-terminal to EVERY glycosylated Ser/Thr, so BOTH bonds here are cut: before Thr192 (P1 = Phe191) and before Thr193 (P1 = the glycosylated Thr192). The paper names only the second because that is the one IMPa cannot make. The first draft of this row encoded the discriminating bond as though it were the whole digest -- caught by running the suite.

IMPa cuts before Thr192, whose P1 (Phe191) is unglycosylated, and is forbidden ONLY the second bond, where P1 is the glycosylated Thr192. Contrast SME-01: same substrate, one fewer cut. The first draft said no cuts at all, which overstated what the paper claims.

DERIVED: STCE-01 extended by one Arg. StcE cuts before S7. Trypsin does NOT cut after Arg1, because Pro2 follows it and trypsin is blocked before proline; Arg10 is C-terminal so severs nothing. TWO products. mzLib's StcE-trypsin motif is 'K|,R|' -- PROLINE-BLIND -- so it also cuts Arg1|Pro2 and returns three. That is a SECOND over-digestion, independent of the glycan one: proteases.tsv reserves the proline rule for the separate 'trypsin|P' entry.
column13: PROLINE. StcE-trypsin uses the proline-BLIND motif K|,R| so it also cuts Arg1|Pro2. The glycan half is now correct: the StcE bond is made only because Thr5 carries a glycan.

column12: Trypsin does not cleave Lys-Pro or Arg-Pro. mzLib's 'trypsin' entry is 'K|,R|' and DOES cut here; the proline-aware entry is named 'trypsin|P' ('K[P]|,R[P]|'). The names are inverted relative to the community convention, where Trypsin/P is the variant that IGNORES proline -- which is what mzLib #1186 is fixing. Encoded against the biological enzyme, so the matching mzLib entry today is trypsin|P.
